thread:
elaine: Quick sync — need a short positioning playbook for the webinar next Tues. Draft below, please annotate. Goal: make it clear how Redwood differs vs cloud AI platforms, LLM API providers, and infra vendors. Also: suggested inbound routing and one-line rebuttals.

matt: Thanks — dropping some quick notes. gonna mark what we should use in slides.

sofia: Love the structure. For the benchmark narrative we should emphasize predictable p99 latency + cost/unit. Cloud vendors win scale, we win predictable per-request economics for production apps.

elaine: Agreed. Draft elevator lines:
```
- For customers using managed cloud AI: "Redwood gives you predictable, production-grade inference with routing and fallbacks so you never choose between latency and cost."
- For teams on LLM APIs: "Same API surface, but with controls to pin models, custom rollout policies, and observability that prevents regressions in production."
- For infra vendors/self-hosted runtimes: "We provide a unified runtime + control plane so you get the benefits of a managed inference stack without re-implementing batching, cache, and cost controls."
```

jordan: Those are tight. Suggest shortening first line for slide header: "Predictable inference — latency, cost, reliability."

noah: Question: for market-facing benchmark claims, do we call out numeric p99s? legal will want evidence. maybe: "<X>ms p50, <Y>ms p95 on common seq lengths" with link to benchmark repo.

elaine: Good call. We'll add an appendix with raw numbers + test harness links. Sofia — can you work with Eng to get the p95/p99 numbers for smallest and largest seq lengths?

sofia: On it. I'll ping eng-runtime and grab the CSV by EOD.

matt: Rebuttal playbook (short):
- "Cloud provider is simpler" -> "True, but our routing, canary rollouts, and per-token cost breakdowns save teams engineering time and money at scale."
- "LLM API is easiest to integrate" -> "We match that simplicity with the same SDK and add enterprise controls — pinning, rollouts, and fallbacks."
- "We can just run the open-source runtime ourselves" -> "You could, but you’d rebuild our observability, smart routing, and cost-reduction tooling — we run this at scale so you don’t have to."

elaine: Perfect. Now inbound lead routing — very pragmatic rules:
- Interest: "SLA / Dedicated capacity" -> route to AE-enterprise + solutions-eng
- Interest: "Pricing / benchmark comparisons" -> product-marketing + growth SDR for follow-up (send benchmark link)
- Interest: "Private / on-prem" -> solutions-eng + security specialist
- Interest: "Quick test / POC" -> growth SDR + technical onboarding doc link

jordan: Can we add an automation snippet for Intercom? Something like: 
```
if (message.contains('on-prem') || message.contains('vpc')) assign('solutions-eng')
else if (message.contains('SLA') || message.contains('dedicated')) assign('AE-enterprise')
else assign('growth-sdr')
```

elaine: Yes. @sam-bot can you wire that into the routing playbook?

sam-bot: queued — will add rules to the routing doc and push a draft for review by 5pm PT. :white_check_mark:

sofia: Also propose a 2-slide appendix for the webinar: 1) Competitive matrix (cols: latency, cost control, deployment modes, observability, rollouts) 2) Quick technical diagram showing smart routing + KV cache + fallback path. I can mock.

matt: I drafted a social copy variant for the launch post — short + link to webinar sign-up. Thoughts?
```
Quick copy: "Ship LLM features with predictable performance. Join our webinar to see benchmarks vs cloud providers and self-hosted runtimes — and how to route traffic for cost & reliability. Register: <link>"
```

elaine: Nice. Two CTA variants: register + request benchmark pack. We'll A/B test in the email.

noah: Final: ownership & deadlines?
- Benchmarks CSV: sofia by EOD today
- Routing automation: sam-bot draft by 5pm PT
- Webinar slides (including comp matrix): matt + sofia draft by Fri noon
- Social copy + email variants: jordan by Fri 3pm

elaine: Thanks all — please add comments inline in the doc I just uploaded. We'll iterate tomorrow morning and lock messaging for the webinar. :sparkles:

matt: Added a quick line about quantization tradeoffs in the technical appendix.

sofia: Uploaded CSV from eng-runtime (link in doc). Moving to update the benchmark slide.

elaine: Closing thread for now — will reopen if any blocking items.
